To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
family firms are associated with a less constrained financial environment than non family firms, especially if the family is part of a network.

family firms, and particularly those belonging to networks, have access to financial markets and to a contract environment that are less restrictive than those faced by non family firms, and that the latter are more constrained in their investment and cash flow decisions.

(1) family firms are less constrained than non family ones; (2) this finding holds in a wide range of specifications, including stratification by bank status, industry, region and time; (3) this finding holds across different financial environments, and (4) this finding is consistent with the predictions of our structural model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of family firms in the economy and how family firms differ from non family firms in terms of financial constraints and access to capital markets.
the relationship between the financial environment and the investment behavior of family firms,
the relationship between the family firm and the financial system, and how this relationship is mediated by the network structure of the family firm.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
family firms are less constrained than non family owned firms, and that family networks are associated with less financial constraints than non-family networks.
family ownership and bank status are important determinants of firm investment and cash-flow.

the financial constraints faced by family firms and their investment behavior are more nuanced and complex than those of non family firms, and the financial constraints faced are not only related to the number of banking relations but also to the nature and structure of the family business network.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

family firms, particularly those that belong to networks, have a better financial environment and are less constrained than non family owned firms, and that the family firm status is more important than bank status in explaining the financial constraints of firms.
family firms are less financially constrained in Spain.

the financial constraints of family firms are not due to a lack of bank credit but rather to a lack of access to a market or a contract environment that allows them to smooth investment and cash flow.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the financial environment of family firms differs from that of non family firms.

family firms are less constrained than non family owned firms, and the reason why they are not constrained is that they are able to access a wider range of financing opportunities, both within their own network and in the market.
family ownership and networks matter for financial constraints, and that these constraints are more important for firms with no bank relations, which are more likely to be smaller firms.
